Current Content: The Plytix MCP is a beta release. To turn it on for your account, contact your account manager. What your assistant can do is limited to the tools in the current release, summarized in Capabilities and permissions. Check the changelog for additions and changes.
Proposed Content: To enable the Plytix MCP beta for your account, contact your account manager. Explore the available tools in Capabilities and permissions, and check the changelog for updates.
Finding / Reason: Keep beta eligibility clear while removing repeated release language and a restrictive introduction.
Validation / Implementation Notes: Keep the existing “Plytix MCP is in beta” callout title. Preserve links to the capabilities page and changelog.

Current Content: This page explains what the Plytix MCP is and how access works, and points you to the guides for connecting your account, the capabilities in this release, example workflows, and troubleshooting.
Proposed Content: This page introduces the Plytix MCP and explains how access works. Use the guides below to connect your AI assistant, explore the available capabilities, try example workflows, and troubleshoot common issues.
Finding / Reason: Use a parallel sequence of actions and a clearer introduction.

Page / Section: Overview / What is the Plytix MCP?
Current Content: Once you connect it, your assistant finds the Plytix tools on its own and calls them when your request needs your account's data. You ask in plain language, and you don't call tools by name.
Proposed Content: After you connect, your AI application discovers the available Plytix tools. Ask your assistant a question or describe a task in natural language. When needed, specify that it should use the Plytix connection.
Finding / Reason: Avoid implying automatic tool use or suggesting users must never mention tools. Align with the verification and troubleshooting guidance.

Current Content: The Plytix MCP isn't an API version, and it doesn't give your assistant every endpoint in the V3 API. It offers the tools summarized in Capabilities and permissions, and that list grows from release to release.
Proposed Content: The Plytix MCP provides tools for working with your catalog through an AI assistant. See Capabilities and permissions for the available operations. Tools may be added, updated, or removed over time, with changes recorded in the changelog.
Finding / Reason: Lead with what the MCP enables. Avoid unnecessary API V3 comparisons and the unsupported promise that the list only grows.
Validation / Implementation Notes: Preserve links to capabilities and changelog. API V3 remains a separately scheduled publication.

Current Content: It's also separate from the Documentation MCP, which reads these docs, needs no account, and can't see your data. Connecting one doesn't connect the other.
Proposed Content: Remove this paragraph from the Platform MCP launch overview.
Finding / Reason: The sentence is grammatical, but it introduces a second service before it is needed or publicly available.
Validation / Implementation Notes: Editorial removal, not a claim that the architecture is incorrect. Reintroduce a comparison separately once the Documentation MCP publication and positioning are confirmed.

Current Content: The Plytix MCP signs in with OAuth, so you authorize your AI application in the browser instead of pasting a token. What your assistant can do depends on the tools in the current release and the access you grant when you authorize the connection.
Proposed Content: You sign in to Plytix with OAuth to authorize your AI application. The available tools and the access granted to the connection determine what your assistant can do.
Finding / Reason: The user signs in, not the MCP server. Use precise authorization language and remove repeated release wording.
Validation / Implementation Notes: Core should confirm the exact permissions applied to the authorized connection. This wording does not imply user-selectable scopes.

Current Content: Follow these guides in order to connect your account and run your first task.
Proposed Content: Start with Connect your AI assistant, verify the connection, and try an example workflow. Use Capabilities and permissions, Troubleshooting, and Changelog as reference guides.
Finding / Reason: Troubleshooting and changelog are reference pages, not compulsory steps in a sequential setup.

Current Content: See what your assistant can do in this release and how access is controlled.
Proposed Content: Explore the available capabilities and learn how access is controlled.
Finding / Reason: Use stable wording that describes the current documentation rather than a particular launch.
Validation / Implementation Notes: Apply this shared card description wherever it appears, including Connect, Example workflows, and Troubleshooting.

Current Content: Fix a connection that fails, missing tools, or answers that don't match your account.
Proposed Content: Resolve connection issues, find missing tools, and investigate unexpected answers.
Finding / Reason: Use parallel actions and avoid suggesting that account data itself is an answer.
Validation / Implementation Notes: Apply consistently to the shared Troubleshooting card on other MCP pages.

Proposed Content: For the Platform MCP launch, show related links to Capabilities and permissions, Example workflows, and Troubleshooting.

Validation / Implementation Notes: The Current Version cell summarizes the visible links. Hide Documentation MCP and API V3 links until their corresponding content is published.

Current Content: To connect, you add the Plytix MCP to your AI application as a remote MCP server, then sign in to Plytix with OAuth to authorize it. This guide has step-by-step instructions for Claude and ChatGPT, and a check to run once you're connected.
Proposed Content: Add the Plytix MCP as a remote MCP server in your AI application, then sign in to Plytix with OAuth. Follow the instructions for Claude or ChatGPT below, then verify the connection.
Finding / Reason: Use direct instructions and identify what “it” refers to.

Current Content: Your application's plan or workspace settings decide whether you can add a custom connection, and a workspace administrator may need to add or approve it first.
Proposed Content: Your subscription plan and workspace settings determine whether you can add a custom connection. A workspace administrator may need to add or approve the connection first.
Finding / Reason: Plans and settings determine availability. Split the sentence for easier scanning.

Current Content: The Plytix MCP is separate from the V3 API, so you don't need V3 or a V3 access token to connect. The OAuth sign-in authorizes your AI application, separately from the access tokens in the API v3 tab.
Proposed Content: You do not need API V3 beta access or an API V3 access token to use the Plytix MCP. Sign in to Plytix with OAuth when your AI application prompts you.
Finding / Reason: Clarify that API V3 access is not a prerequisite. Avoid ambiguous wording about not needing “V3.”
Validation / Implementation Notes: Use plain text for the API V3 reference until its authentication documentation is publicly available.

Current Content: Pick your AI application and follow the steps to add the server, authorize it, and turn it on in a conversation.
Proposed Content: Select your AI application and follow the steps to add the server, authorize the connection, and enable it in a conversation.
Finding / Reason: Use distinct, consistent terms for configuration, authorization, and conversation activation.

Current Content: Owners add it in Organization settings > Connectors by clicking Add, hovering over Custom, and selecting Web, then entering the name and server URL as in steps 3 to 5 below. After that, each member connects with their own Plytix sign-in: go to Customize > Connectors, find Plytix, click Connect, and continue from step 6.
Proposed Content:
Organization setup: An owner or another user with connector-management permissions adds Plytix in Organization settings > Connectors.
Member sign-in: Open Customize > Connectors, select Plytix, click Connect, and sign in to your own Plytix account.
Finding / Reason: Separate administrator setup from member sign-in. Cross-referencing steps for a different role makes the procedure difficult to follow.
Validation / Implementation Notes: Place the existing full configuration steps under Organization setup as a separate numbered list. Preserve the documented role distinctions and verify actual UI labels before publication.

Current Content: To disconnect, go to Customize > Connectors, find Plytix, and click Remove or the three dots next to it.
Proposed Content: To remove the connection, open Customize > Connectors and find Plytix. Select Remove, or open its three-dot menu and select the removal option. Complete any confirmation prompts.
Finding / Reason: Opening a menu does not complete removal. Describe the final action.
Validation / Implementation Notes: Verify the final removal label in the supported Claude UI. Do not equate local removal with revoking every authorization in Plytix without Core confirmation.

Current Content: Review each request before you approve it, and only remember an approval for a tool you trust to change your catalog without asking.
Proposed Content: Review each tool request before approving it. Choose to remember an approval only if you trust the tool to make further changes without another review. Remembered approvals apply within the conversation, subject to ChatGPT’s current behavior.
Finding / Reason: Clarify who selects the remembered-approval option and its scope.
Validation / Implementation Notes: Keep behavior aligned with OpenAI’s current documentation: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/custom-mcp-server

Current Content: A working connection answers with the capabilities in this release. This confirms that the tools were found, but not that your assistant can read your data.
Proposed Content: Use the tool list in your AI application’s connection settings to check which tools were discovered. Then verify access to your account with the product lookup below. An answer describing capabilities alone does not confirm a successful connection.
Finding / Reason: A plausible assistant response is not evidence that discovery or a tool call succeeded.

Current Content: Using Plytix, find the product with SKU GF-Basket and show its name and description.
Proposed Content:
Replace YOUR-SKU with a SKU that exists in your account, then ask:
Using Plytix, find the product with SKU YOUR-SKU and show its SKU, name, and description. Do not change anything.
Finding / Reason: An unexplained sample SKU can produce an empty result even when the connection works.
Validation / Implementation Notes: Keep the replacement instruction immediately above the copyable prompt.

Current Content: This page summarizes what your assistant can do with the Plytix MCP in this release, and what controls the access it has. It's a summary, not a tool reference: the Plytix MCP describes each of its tools to your AI application directly.
Proposed Content: This page summarizes the capabilities available in the current version of the Plytix MCP and explains how access is controlled. Your AI application discovers individual tool descriptions and input schemas directly from the server.
Finding / Reason: Use natural wording and explain the page’s relationship to self-describing tools.

Current Content: Capabilities in this release
Proposed Content: Available capabilities
Finding / Reason: A stable heading avoids unnecessary launch-specific language.

Current Content: Limitations
Proposed Content: Usage notes
Finding / Reason: Use a neutral, practical heading for operational details.
Validation / Implementation Notes: Keep meaningful pagination, static-list membership, and irreversible-deletion information. The heading change must not conceal real restrictions.

Current Content: The tool list can change from one release to the next. Some AI applications keep the list they got when you connected, so after a release you may need to refresh the connection, or remove it and connect again, before your assistant sees new or changed tools. To see the exact tools available to you, check the connection in your application's settings or ask your assistant. The changelog says when a release needs you to refresh.
Proposed Content: Available tools may change over time. Some AI applications cache the tool list, so refresh it after an update when your application supports this. If refreshing does not update the list, follow the application’s reconnection instructions. Check the connection settings for the tools currently available. The changelog identifies updates that require action.
Finding / Reason: Avoid casual wording, repeated release references, and removal as the immediate default.

Current Content: The tools in the current release. Your assistant can only do what the tools in Capabilities in this release cover.
Proposed Content: Available tools. Your assistant can use the operations described in Available capabilities, subject to the connection’s access and your AI application’s controls.
Finding / Reason: Align the terminology with the renamed heading and retain the other access conditions.

Current Content: For example, Claude asks for your approval before it runs a tool, lets you allow a tool always, and lets you turn tools off in a conversation. ChatGPT asks you to confirm write actions and lets you turn individual tools on or off.
Proposed Content: AI applications offer different tool controls. Claude provides approval options such as Allow always and controls for disabling tools in a conversation. ChatGPT provides tool controls and confirmation settings for write actions. See Connect your AI assistant for the application-specific steps.
Finding / Reason: Correct the awkward “allow a tool always” phrasing and avoid universal approval guarantees.
Validation / Implementation Notes: Match exact controls and approval scope to the supported clients. Do not rename literal UI labels.

Current Content: If your application has no per-tool controls, any tool can run when your assistant calls it.
Proposed Content: If your AI application does not provide per-tool controls, tool access is governed by the authorization granted to the connection and the restrictions enforced by Plytix.
Finding / Reason: The current sentence overlooks authorization and server-side restrictions.
Validation / Implementation Notes: Core confirmation required: document the actual permissions and restrictions enforced by the Platform MCP before publishing this wording.

Current Content: These prompts describe tasks you might hand to your assistant once you've connected your account. Each one names what it needs from the release, so skip any that the current capabilities don't cover. Start your prompt with "Using Plytix," so your assistant knows to call the Plytix tools, then adapt the SKUs and fields to your own catalog.
Proposed Content: Use these prompts as starting points after connecting your account. Replace sample SKUs, category names, and attribute labels with values from your own catalog. Each example identifies the capabilities it requires. Specify that the assistant should use Plytix, and check the resulting tool calls and data.
Finding / Reason: Provide curated examples with explicit prerequisites. Avoid implying that the published guide knowingly includes unsupported examples.
Validation / Implementation Notes: Validate each example against the available tools before publication. Do not present prompt wording as a guarantee of tool selection.

Current Content: Using Plytix, compare the attached supplier file with my catalog. List the SKUs in the file that aren't in Plytix, and the SKUs whose name differs from Plytix. Don't change anything.
Proposed Content: Using Plytix, compare the attached supplier file with my catalog. List the SKUs that are missing from Plytix and the SKUs of products whose names differ between the file and the catalog. Report how many rows you checked and any rows you could not compare. Do not change anything.
Finding / Reason: Compare product names across the two sources and make review coverage visible.

Current Content: For a long file, ask how many SKUs it checked and compare that with the file.
Proposed Content: For a large file, compare the number of rows reviewed with the total number of rows supplied. Ask the assistant to identify duplicate SKUs, skipped rows, and any records it could not compare.
Finding / Reason: Specify comparable counts and expose incomplete processing.

Current Content: Using Plytix, which category is SKU GF-Basket in, and what does its description say? Show the values you used.
Proposed Content: Using Plytix, list the categories assigned to SKU YOUR-SKU and show its description. Include the SKU and the values returned by Plytix. Do not change anything.
Finding / Reason: Allow for multiple category assignments and use a clearly replaceable SKU.
Validation / Implementation Notes: Use the shared instruction to replace YOUR-SKU with an existing product.

Current Content: Your assistant reads the current description and shows you a suggested rewrite. Nothing changes in Plytix until you approve the text in a second prompt, such as "Save that description to GF-Basket."
Proposed Content: For this workflow, ask the assistant to read the description and propose a rewrite without saving it. Review the proposal before asking it to update the product. A write tool applies the update when it executes, subject to your AI application’s controls.
Finding / Reason: Present proposal and approval as a recommended sequence, not an MCP-enforced guarantee.

Page / Section: Examples / Scope of a description update
Current Content: Saving the text updates the value of the description attribute on that one product. It doesn't change the description attribute itself, so other products and the attribute's settings stay as they are. This step needs the tool that updates products.
Proposed Content: Saving the text updates the product’s description value through the product-update tool. It does not edit the attribute definition. Confirm how parent and variant inheritance applies before updating an inherited value.
Finding / Reason: Keep the distinction between values and definitions, without guaranteeing that every related product is unaffected.
Validation / Implementation Notes: Core confirmation required: verify inheritance and propagation behavior. This is a validation item, not a confirmed defect in the MCP.

Current Content: The Plytix MCP is in beta, so its capabilities are limited to the tools in the current release, and an action that isn't in Capabilities and permissions isn't available yet. Your assistant also reads product data from suppliers, imports, and integrations. Treat that text as untrusted, and keep reading and writing in separate prompts.
Proposed Content: Use the checks below to investigate connection issues, missing tools, and unexpected results. See Capabilities and permissions for the supported operations. When reviewing catalog or supplier content, treat it as data rather than instructions. Request proposed changes separately before asking the assistant to save them.
Finding / Reason: Lead with the purpose of troubleshooting and explain “untrusted” in concrete terms. Avoid repeated beta and release framing.

Current Content: Check that the server URL matches https://pim.plytix.com/mcp exactly, then complete the OAuth authorization again. If your application asks for an administrator's approval for custom connections, the connection can't finish until that approval is given.
Proposed Content: Confirm that MCP beta access is enabled for your Plytix account and that the server URL is https://pim.plytix.com/mcp. Check any required workspace approval, then retry OAuth sign-in. If the connection still fails, contact your account manager or Plytix support with the application name and the error message. Do not include tokens or passwords.
Finding / Reason: Include beta eligibility and an actionable escalation route.

Current Content: The changelog says when a release needs you to refresh.
Proposed Content: The changelog indicates when you need to refresh your tool list.
Finding / Reason: Replace an unnatural construction while keeping release terminology where it describes an actual update.

Current Content: An answer that sounds plausible but doesn't match your account usually means your assistant answered from its own knowledge instead of calling a tool. Start the prompt with "Using Plytix," and ask your assistant to show the SKUs it retrieved, so you can check the answer against Plytix.
Proposed Content: Inspect the tool-call details to check whether the assistant used Plytix. Verify the connected account, requested SKU, returned fields, and any pagination. Ask the assistant to show the retrieved values and distinguish them from its own interpretation.
Finding / Reason: Do not assign a single likely cause without checking the evidence.

Current Content: Results are shorter than what Plytix shows
Proposed Content: Fewer results are returned than expected
Finding / Reason: Use a heading about record counts, rather than text length.

Current Content: Your assistant may have stopped at the first page of results and reported it as the full answer. Ask it to get all the results, and include the expected count in your prompt when you know it, so your assistant can check its answer against that count.
Proposed Content: The assistant may have retrieved only part of the result set. Ask it to follow pagination, report the number of records retrieved, and identify any remaining pages or processing limits. If you know the expected count, compare it with the reported total. A request for all results does not by itself confirm completeness.
Finding / Reason: Explain how to establish coverage instead of suggesting that a prompt alone guarantees it.

Proposed Content: Usage notes: The initial beta supports product data, assets, and the catalog structures described in Capabilities and permissions. Channel management is outside the supported scope.
